post.description:
Detect dependency cycles and gate on newly-introduced ones.

This is the DOING-side architecture-delta gate. The QA ``verify-architecture``
oracle hard-fails on ANY cycle (absolute); this endpoint instead reports a
*delta* so a behavior-preserving refactor is blocked only when it introduces
a cycle that was not present before — pre-existing unrelated cycles do not
block the refactor in DOING (QA remains the absolute backstop).

Report mode (no ``baseline_cycles``): returns the current cycle signatures so
the caller can capture a pre-refactor baseline. Always ``success=True``. It
FORCE-REBUILDS the graph first — see ``_ensure_graph_populated``; without that
the baseline describes a stale tree and the gate below can never fail.

Both modes carry provenance: ``grounded`` / ``ungrounded_reason`` /
``graph_built`` / ``component_count`` / ``node_count``. ``grounded=False`` means
no usable graph was read, so the result is absence of evidence — graders must
abstain on it rather than treat it as a clean pass.

Gate mode (``baseline_cycles`` supplied): returns ``success=False`` when the
current graph contains a cycle signature absent from the baseline. The HTTP
status stays 200; the ``success`` flag is the gate the DOING orchestrator
reads (a ``success=False`` coding step is a hard BLOCK).

post.description:
Run synchronous quality analysis and return results directly.

When ``container_name`` is given the run is also STORED (``quality_results``)
and the response carries ``result_id`` / ``commit_sha`` / ``persisted``.
Persistence never fails the response: this route is an auto-run verifier,
and every pre-existing key is unchanged.

Inline ``code_content`` without ``container_name`` is a 422
(``INLINE_CODE_NEEDS_WORKSPACE``) and executes nothing: every tool runs via
coding-containers exec inside the workspace container, and this pod has
no tools of its own, so an ad-hoc run could only ever come back
"inconclusive: 0/N tools succeeded". Send ``container_name`` (+ ``paths``).
With ``container_name`` set, ``code_content`` is ignored.

``paths`` (with ``container_name``) scopes the run to those
workspace-relative files/directories: only they are fetched from the
container and fed to the tools, and only their issues are reported. The
response echoes the scope as ``scope`` (``null`` for a whole-workspace run).
A scope that matches no source file is a 422 ("paths match no files"),
never an empty-but-successful report. Absolute paths, ``..`` and more than
``MAX_SCOPE_PATHS`` entries are 422 at validation.

Store decision: a SCOPED run is NOT stored (``persisted: false``). The
``quality_results`` row has no scope column, and ``/{c}/latest``,
``/{c}/gate`` and ``/{c}/history`` read the newest row for the container
as its full-workspace result — storing a one-file run would silently
replace the container's gate verdict with a partial one.

get.description:
Evaluate quality gate criteria against the container's CURRENT commit.

The gate is called by the upgrade procedure's ``verify_quality_gate`` step
right after it changes code, with no analyze call first — so it must grade
the commit that is checked out NOW, never an older stored run:

- resolve the container's HEAD sha (bounded, 5s);
- a stored row for (tenant, container, that sha) → grade it, no analysis
  (``source: "stored"``);
- otherwise (no row for this sha, or the sha is unresolvable) → run the
  analyzer, persist the run (a persist failure never fails the gate) and
  grade the fresh result (``source: "analyzed"``).

The gate passes only if ALL checks pass AND the graded run is ``complete``:
a failed run, an inconclusive run and a partial run (graded on a subset of
tools) can never pass. This is the ONLY quality GET that may analyze.

post.description: Commit changes to git in the container.

Put HEAD on local branch ``branch``; idempotent, never destructive.

WHY THIS EXISTS. Callers used a raw ``exec`` of ``git checkout -B <branch>``, which
RESETS an existing branch to the current HEAD and so silently drops its commits.

- ``refs/heads/<branch>`` exists -> ``git switch --no-guess <branch>``. Uncommitted
  changes carry over; if git refuses (they would be overwritten, unmerged index,
  branch checked out in another worktree) the answer is 409
  ``branch_switch_conflict`` and nothing has changed - git checks before it writes,
  and the route re-measures HEAD to confirm it.
- absent -> ``git switch --no-track -c <branch>`` from the current HEAD, including
  a detached one (``previous_branch`` is then ``null``).
- Never ``checkout -B``, ``--force``, ``--discard-changes``, ``--merge`` or ``reset``.

The name must pass ``_validate_git_branch_name`` (400, before any command runs)
and ``git check-ref-format --branch`` (400, before any mutation). A workspace with
no commit yet is a 400. ``branch`` and ``head_sha`` in the response are measured
after the switch; a switch that exits 0 but leaves HEAD elsewhere is a 500. So is
one that exits 0 but leaves a path of the new tree unwritten (a missing blob):
500 ``branch_switch_incomplete``, measured as tracked paths modified in the
worktree (``ls-files --modified``: missing or stale content) after the switch
that were not already modified before it.

400.description: Invalid branch name or not running

409.description: branch_switch_conflict: git refused the switch; nothing changed

post.description: Read CI state for a PR's head commit. **`verdict` is three-valued** — `passed` | `failed` | `pending`. Never infer `passed` from `failed == 0`: an unrun pipeline has no failures. `passed` requires every check COMPLETED, no failing conclusion, and at least `expected_checks` (default 1) runs with conclusion `success`; skipped/neutral runs never count toward it. Every name in `required_checks` must have a latest run concluding `success`.

post.summary: Wait for a PR's checks to finish (202 + completion callback)
post.description:
Pin the PR's current head SHA and return immediately with a wait id. When every
    check run and commit status on that SHA has completed, the result is POSTed once to
    `callback_url` (an n8n Wait-node resume URL): `overall` = `success` | `failure` |
    `skipped`, with each check's name, conclusion and url.

    It also resolves — never parks forever — when the head moves (`superseded` +
    `new_head_sha`), the PR is closed unmerged before CI settles (`pr_closed`), the SHA
    has no checks and none will come (`no_checks`: no active workflow, or no check
    suite created for the SHA within the stale window), a workflow fails to start
    (`failure`), required/expected checks never appear once CI finished (`failure`
    with `missing` items), or GitHub says
    the PR can no longer be read (`error`). No polling: evaluated at registration, on
    GitHub's check/status/workflow/PR deliveries for the repository, and at startup.
    `GET /ci-wait/{wait_id}` reads the same document.

GitHubFileChangeOperation.title: GitHubFileChangeOperation
GitHubFileChangeOperation.description:
Model representing a single file change operation for GitHub API.

    This model describes a change to be applied to a file in a repository,
    supporting various change types including additions, modifications,
    deletions, and renames.

    Attributes:
        file_path (str): Path to the file relative to repository root
        content (Optional[str]): New content for the file. Required for
            "added"/"modified"/"renamed"; omitted for "deleted".
        change_type (str): Type of change ("added", "modified", "deleted", "renamed")
        old_file_path (Optional[str]): Original path for rename operations

    Example:
        ```python
        # Modify existing file
        change = FileChange(
            file_path="src/main.py",
            content="def main():
    print('Hello, World!')
",
            change_type="modified"
        )

        # Rename file
        rename_change = FileChange(
            file_path="src/new_main.py",
            content="def main():
    print('Hello, World!')
",
            change_type="renamed",
            old_file_path="src/main.py"
        )

        # Delete a file (no content)
        delete_change = FileChange(
            file_path="src/dead_code.py",
            change_type="deleted"
        )
        ```

    Note:
        For rename operations, both old_file_path and file_path must be provided.
        The content field should contain the final content after the rename.
        A delete carries no content; every other change_type requires it.

    ⛔ ``change_type`` is a CLOSED set, and must stay closed.
        ``GitHubIntegration._apply_changes`` branches on these four exact
        strings and ends in an ``else`` that treats anything unrecognised as a
        CONTENT WRITE. This field previously carried only
        ``pattern=SAFE_STRING_PATTERN`` — ``^[\s\S]*$``, which every string
        satisfies — so the singular ``"delete"`` validated, fell to that
        ``else``, and overwrote the file it was asked to remove, logging a
        warning and reporting success.

        That spelling is not hypothetical: the change spec is LLM-generated and
        ``AA_IMPLEMENTATION/doing_action_procedures.json`` forwards
        ``generate_code_change_spec.output.changes`` verbatim. n8n's worker
        prompt has to tell the model outright that ``"delete"``, ``"remove"``
        and ``"removed"`` are NOT recognised — which is exactly the evidence
        that a model reaches for them. Widening this back to ``str`` restores a
        silent data-destroying path; a typo must be a 422, never a write.

When set, a push touching any other path is refused (path_not_in_target_files). Process data (.aa/, *_probe/, *.log, ...) is refused whether or not this is set.

When set, EVERY path the pushed commits touch must be a key here, and its blob at the pushed tip must equal the value, or the push is refused (push_content_unverified / push_content_mismatch). REQUIRED when `target_files` is set: an allowlist of paths alone lets a workspace that faked the reviewed diff ship other content in an allowed file.

approved_tree.description: The reviewed tree (a `git/diff` response's `tree`). When set, the push sends EXACTLY ONE commit: its only parent must be the commit the remote already has (the base GitHub reports) and its tree must be this id, or the push is refused (push_not_single_commit / push_tree_mismatch). Tree-id equality binds every byte pushed, and an intermediate commit (evil content added, then reverted) can never ride along. REQUIRED when `target_files` or `target_blobs` is set.

ValidationErrorResponse.title: ValidationErrorResponse
ValidationErrorResponse.description:
Specialized error response for request validation failures.

This model extends StandardErrorResponse to provide detailed information
about validation errors, including field-level error details. It's used
when request data fails Pydantic model validation.

Attributes:
    status (ResponseStatus): Always 'error' for validation errors
    message (str): Default "Request validation failed"
    error_code (str): Default "VALIDATION_ERROR"
    validation_errors (List[APIValidationErrorDetail]): List of field-specific errors

Example:
    ```python
    validation_error = ValidationErrorResponse(
        path="/api/users",
        request_id="req_123456",
        validation_errors=[
            APIValidationErrorDetail(
                field="email",
                message="Invalid email format",
                type="format_error",
                input="not-an-email"
            ),
            APIValidationErrorDetail(
                field="age",
                message="Age must be a positive integer",
                type="type_error",
                input=-5
            )
        ]
    )
    ```

Note:
    This response type is typically returned with HTTP status code 422
    (Unprocessable Entity) to indicate validation failures.

    message (str): Human-readable description of the validation failure

    ```python
        field="age",
        message="Age must be between 0 and 150",
        type="range_error",
        input=200
    )
    ```

    The field path uses dot notation for nested fields (e.g., "address.zipcode").
    The input value is included to help with debugging but may be omitted
    for sensitive fields like passwords.
